Fernando Mendoza is an extremely productive QB from Indiana. He has an excellent frame and adequate athleticism for the position. He displays good arm talent, with the ability to make almost any throw on the field, and he is extremely accurate and smart. His best qualities are being able to put the ball on the money to receivers in stride and his ability to get the ball out quickly. He needs to improve his pocket mobility and awareness, and he needs to show the ability to adapt to new schemes. Overall, he will be an NFL starter.

Ty Simpson is an accurate quarterback from Alabama. He is slightly undersized but is athletic and smart. He plays with excellent timing on his dropback and hits receivers in stride with excellent accuracy and field vision. He has really good arm talent, with the ability to put the ball on all three levels accurately. He also has a quick release. He is great in the pocket and has adequate athleticism to escape and occasionally gain some yardage. He is not an elite player out of structure, and he can stare down receivers occasionally.

As a passer, he displays a special arm talent, with pace from any arm slot and footwork. He can put touch on the ball and has decent accuracy. His biggest issues come from his mental side. He struggles under pressure and often makes poor decisions. In addition, his mechanics break down, leading to negative plays. He has excellent athleticism and scrambling ability and gets tough yards.

He is a developmental player.

His skinny frame may raise concerns, but he is extremely muscular and has the strength to quiet any criticisms. He thrives when able to run behind the lineman and pick his hole. I believe an outside zone scheme would fit him.

Emmett Johnson is a feisty running back from Nebraska. He has solid size for the position and uses it well. He is a threat in both the ground and air game. He is a very tough runner who runs through contact very well. His best quality is his agility and his nasty jump cut. He dashes through holes and plays at full effort on every rep. As a blocker, he is very poor, which limits his 3-down upside in the NFL. He also has some concerns about his long speed, as he can get caught from behind (Iowa). Overall he will be an NFL contributor.

He is very bursty and can get short yards quickly, but his breakaway ability is poor, and he doesn’t have great speed. He is a willing blocker but needs to work on his technique. He can be a committee back with some upside.

Kaytron Allen is a productive runner from Penn State.  He has a big frame and uses it well. He is a power back who always falls forward on his runs and wins with his combination of balance and strength. He is very patient and displays good vision. In terms of a big play running back, Kaytron is probably not your guy. He lacks top end speed or agility and often looks slow, especially when there is no clear gap in the line. He needs to increase his passing game usage and blocking ability to maximize his ability. He can definitely have a role in the NFL.

His lateral agility is something to behold, but he needs to be in space to use it. He is not especially good in the receiving or blocking game. He can succeed when given space to work with but he is not an all-around back.

He does need to work against press coverage and more outside to give him more versatility, as 70% of his plays are in the slot.

If he stays healthy, he can be a top option for a team.
